title: Vector RAG failure modes (relationship data, similarity vs relevance, explainability, maturity)
keyFindings: The suite's graph-first architecture already mitigates the relationship-data and maturity failure modes: Astrographer's documents are Provident graphs with a fact/reference/embed model (astrographer.md §4.2) and Zodiac pre-graphs crawled data (zodiac.md §4.2), so relationship data is captured at the substrate, not left to a vector index.

The similarity-vs-relevance gap is addressed by structural relevance signals (Incanter's graph-tension + vector hybrid, incanter.md §4.8; Zodiac's graph/vector/hybrid modes, zodiac.md §4.3.2) but the exact-match lexical (BM25) leg for factKey/title/tags is still missing — GAP-2 / parked D5.

Explainability is the strongest concrete gap: the consistency model already tracks every link/embed to its target (astrographer.md §4.2.3) and ragQuery already returns {documentId, nodeId, source}, so adding a trace path to RAG results is a cheap, high-value extension that answers the governance/sourcing point.
Maturity argues for keeping the graph layer primary and treating vector as an additive index, consistent with D2 (local-first, no heavy cloud vector DB) and D1 (AGPL, no proprietary vector service).

The expensive global techniques (community summaries, dynamic graph query generation) stay PARKED for D2 cost reasons, consistent with the DAG-RAG research's DISCARD of pre-built global graph construction.

Mystery's topic→reference crosslink resolution (pending #12) is a relationship-mapping problem that vectors miss; model it as graph edges over Astrographer's reference graph when the Mystery contract is written.
summary: The four vector-RAG failure modes (relationship data, similarity vs relevance, explainability, maturity) are the justification for the suite's graph-first architecture, not a new technique to add. Astrographer and Zodiac are already graphical RAG engines over knowledge-graph-shaped data, which addresses the relationship-data and maturity failure modes. The concrete MUST/SHOULD work is graph-enhanced retrieval over the reference graph, an explainability/trace surface on RAG results, and the lexical leg for the similarity-vs-relevance gap; the expensive global techniques stay PARKED for D2 cost reasons.
